In PHP, boolean array keys are cast to integers: true becomes 1 and false becomes 0.

The dependency rule in Clean/Onion Architecture states that source code dependencies must always point inward toward the center (the domain), meaning inner layers must not depend on outer layers.

Controllers and Twig templates belong to the presentation/interface layer, not the business-logic layer; they simply call use cases to translate between HTTP and the application.
In onion architecture, the domain (enterprise business rules) sits at the very center, with all other layers depending on it, not the other way around.
Deptrac and similar tools analyze inter-layer dependencies and report a failure when a forbidden dependency rule is violated, enabling automated enforcement of layer boundaries.
A use case should be decoupled from infrastructure; it should work with domain entities and use ports/abstractions, not concrete HTTP requests or EntityManagers.
The Repository pattern provides a collection of aggregates/entities while hiding the storage mechanism behind an interface, acting like an in-memory collection of domain objects.
In Clean Architecture, the database is an outermost-layer detail (framework/driver) that implements a port defined by the use cases; swapping it doesn't affect the domain or use case logic.

DDD recommends rich domain models where business logic is encapsulated in entities and value objects, not separated into service layers.
In Domain-Driven Design, a Bounded Context defines a boundary within which a specific model is valid, so the same real-world concept can be modeled as a different class in different contexts.

MVCC in PostgreSQL is designed so that readers do NOT block writers and writers do NOT block readers; that's the whole point of multi-version concurrency control.
